text: Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go aside. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever he shows me I will tell you." So he went off to a barren height.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have set up seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram."
The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and speak this."
So he returned to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the officials of Moab.

Then Balaam took up his oracle and said:
"From Aram Balak brought me,
the king of Moab, from the eastern mountains:
'Come, curse Jacob for me;
come, denounce Israel.'

How can I curse those whom God has not cursed?
How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?

versions.text:
How can I curse what God has not cursed?
How can I denounce what the LORD has not denounced?
versions.explanation: The object of the cursing is a people (Jacob/Israel), not a thing. English 'what' suggests an impersonal object; 'those whom' is both grammatically and contextually accurate, and it reads naturally aloud.

text:
From the rocky peaks I see them,
from the heights I behold them:
a people living apart,
not reckoning themselves among the nations.

Who can count the dust of Jacob
or number even a fourth of Israel?
Let me die the death of the upright,
and let my end be like theirs!"

versions.text:
Who can count the dust of Jacob
or number the multitudes of Israel?
Let me die the death of the upright,
and let my end be like theirs!"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew rova' means 'fourth part' (or possibly 'dust cloud'); 'multitudes' loses the concrete image of the parallel line. If 'multitudes' is retained, a footnote noting 'Hebrew: the fourth part' would help the reader.

text: Then Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and instead you have blessed them—blessed them completely!"
He answered, "Must I not say only what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Then Balak said to him, "Come with me to another place, where you can see them. You will see only part of them, not all of them—curse them for me from there."
So he took him to the field of Zophim, on the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go over there to meet the LORD."

versions.text: Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet with him over there."
versions.explanation: The pronoun 'him' has no clear antecedent in this verse (the nearest noun is 'burnt offering'), which is confusing when read aloud. Naming the LORD matches the sense of the Hebrew verb (to be met by God) and parallels verse 3.

text: The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, saying, "Go back to Balak and speak this."
So he came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering with the officials of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"

God is not a man, that he should lie,
nor a son of man, that he should change his mind.
Does he speak and then not act?
Does he promise and not fulfill?

I have been given a word of blessing;
he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.

He has seen no iniquity in Jacob,
and observed no trouble in Israel.
The LORD their God is with them;
the shout of a king is among them.

versions.text:
He has seen no iniquity in Jacob,
no wrongdoing observed in Israel.
The LORD their God is with them;
the shout of a king is among them.
versions.explanation: The second line shifts awkwardly into a subjectless passive, breaking the poetic parallelism of the Hebrew, where God is the subject of both verbs. An active parallel line reads better aloud.

text:
God brought them out of Egypt;
they have the strength of a wild ox.

There is no sorcery against Jacob,
no divination against Israel.
Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel:
'See what God has done!'

Look, a people rises like a lioness;
like a lion it rears itself up.
It does not lie down until it has devoured its prey
and drunk the blood of the slain."
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, then—but do not bless them either!"
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you that I must do whatever the LORD says?"
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
